sanskrit: sa devān āgacchat taṃ devā abruvann āśaṃsāmahe gurv etad vratam āraṇyeṣu paśuṣu grāmyeṣv aty eti
english: He came to the gods; the gods said to him: 'We commend this heavy vow — it surpasses both the wild beasts in the forest and the domestic cattle in the village.'

sanskrit: so 'naḍvāham upādhāvat tam anaḍvān abravīt kiṃ me pratīvāho bhaviṣyatīti varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti sa varam avṛṇīta
english: He approached the bull (anaḍvāh). The bull said to him: 'What shall be my recompense?' He replied: 'Choose a boon.' And so he chose a boon.
'May I be in the world of Bradhna; may I rest upon the summit of Bradhna' — thus he chose.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśo vā ita ūrdhvo loko yad bradhno yad bradhnasya viṣṭapaḥ
english: The world that is Bradhna, the summit of Bradhna — that world is the sixteenth above this one.

sanskrit: bradhnaloko bhavati bradhnasya viṣṭapi śrayate yaḥ (…)
english: He who [observes this vow] attains the world of Bradhna and rests upon the summit of Bradhna.

sanskrit: athāhīnā āśvatthir abravīn na tād brāhmaṇaṃ nindāni yād enam aśṛṇon ned iṣṭāpūrtena vi bhavānīti
english: Then the serpent Āśvatthī said: 'I will not reproach that brahmin whom I heard thus — lest I be cut off from his accumulated merit of rites and pious works.'

sanskrit: kṛtyā vā eṣā manuṣyeṣu carati yad anaḍvān yad anaḍudvratī
english: For it is indeed a powerful rite (kṛtyā) that moves among men — namely the bull, namely the one who observes the bull-vow.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ viduṣo 'sādhu kīrtayati- -iṣṭam evāsya pūrtaṃ māyāṃ saṃ vṛkte
english: Whoever speaks ill of one who knows this — that person's own accumulated rites and pious works are swept away by illusion.

sanskrit: indro vā agre asureṣv anaḍudvratam acarat teṣām iṣṭaṃ pūrtaṃ māyāṃ saṃvṛktānindraṃ hy enam
english: Indeed, Indra first practised the bull-vow among the Asuras; he swept away their rites and pious works into illusion — for they (had wrongly) called him 'non-Indra'.
He stepped onto the back of the bull and came to know all the worlds.

sanskrit: yāv asya pūrvapādau tau pūrvapakṣau yāv aparapādau tāv aparapakṣau
english: The bull's two fore-legs are the two fortnights of the waxing moon; the two hind-legs are the two fortnights of the waning moon.

sanskrit: yāv asyauṣṭhau tau puroḍāśau ye nāsike tau sruvau
english: His two lips are the two sacrificial cake-offerings (puroḍāśa); his two nostrils are the two sacrificial ladles (sruva).

sanskrit: ye asyākṣau tau sūryācandramasau ye nimeṣās tāny ahorātrāṇi yāni vakṣaṇāni te sūryasya raśmayaḥ saḥ (…)
english: His two eyes are the sun and the moon; his blinks are the days and nights; his flanks are the rays of the sun. He who [observes this vow thus attains all worlds].
The droṇa-vessel is his head; King Soma is his brain.

sanskrit: ye asya śṛṅge tad ṛtaṃ satyam
english: His two horns are cosmic order (ṛta) and truth (satya).

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ vā ṛtaṃ satyaṃ tasmād ete dhruve
english: Cosmic order and truth are indeed fixed (dhruva); therefore these two horns are firm.

sanskrit: dhruvam eva rtaṃ satyam anu prati tiṣṭhati yaḥ (…)
english: He who [knows this] stands firm, in accord with the fixed reality of cosmic order and truth.

sanskrit: carācarā vai śraddhā tasmāt karṇau muhur varīvarjayati
english: Faith (śraddhā) is indeed both moving and still; therefore one repeatedly inclines the ears again and again [to hear it].
He who [knows this] becomes worthy of faith — people place their faith in him.
